chunks: Salih ibn Isa ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Ijli narrated to us. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ali narrated to us. He said: Abu Nasr al-Sha'rani narrated to us in the mosque of Humayd. He said: Salama ibn al-Waddah narrated to us from his father, from Abu Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, from Asim ibn Damra, from al-Harith al-A'war. He said:

While I was walking with the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) in al-Hira, we came upon a monk striking the bell. Ali said: O Harith, do you know what this bell says? I said: God, His Messenger and the son of His Messenger's uncle know best. He said: It strikes the parable of the world and its ruin, saying: There is no god but God, truly, sincerely. The world deceived, occupied, lured, and misled us. O son of the world, slowly! Beat by beat! Gathering! The world perishes generation after generation. Each day weakens a pillar. We wasted the enduring abode and settled in the perishing. We do not know what we neglected until we die. Harith asked: Do Christians know? He said: If they knew they would not have deified Christ. I went to the monk, he struck the bell, I recited word by word. He accepted Islam and said: I found in the Torah that among the last prophets there would be one who interprets the bell.

key_terms.الحيرة: Al-Hira - ancient Lakhmid capital near Kufa, a major Christian center in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Iraq
key_terms.الناقوس: Al-Naqus - the church bell (naqus), used by Eastern Christians instead of a call to prayer
key_terms.يا ابن الدنيا مهلا مهلا: Ya ibn al-dunya mahlan mahlan - O son of the world, slowly, slowly! A poetic personification addressing humanity as children of the temporal world

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say the church bell says?
ai.summary: Al-Harith al-A'war recounts walking with Imam Ali through the Christian city of al-Hira when they encountered a monk ringing a church bell. Ali asked Harith if he knew what the bell was saying, then revealed that its pealing was a lament about worldly deception -- a poetic admonition to heedless humanity that echoes 'la ilaha illa Allah' and warns that each passing day weakens a pillar of our being while we waste the eternal abode for the transient one. When Harith asked if Christians knew this hidden meaning, Ali replied that had they understood it, they would never have deified Christ. Harith then tested the revelation by asking the monk to ring the bell while he recited the interpretation word by word, and the astonished monk confirmed the interpretation, accepted Islam, and revealed that the Torah had foretold a final prophet who would interpret the bell's message.

en.bilal-muhammad: Salih b. `Isa b. Ahmad b Muhammad al-`Ijli narrated to us. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad b. `Ali b. `Ali narrated to us. He said: Abu Nasr al-Sha`rani narrated to us in Masjid Hamid. He said: Salama b. al-Wadah narrated to us from his father from Abi Isra’il from Abi Ishaq al-Hamadani from `Asim b. Damra from al-Harith al-A`war.  He said:

I was with Amir al-Mu’minin `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) in Hira when we came across a monk striking the bell of his monastery. So, `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) said: O Harith! Do you know what this bell is saying? I said: Allah, His Messenger, and the cousin of His Messenger know best. He said: He strikes like this world and its ruin, and it says: “There is no god but Allah, truly, truly, verily, verily. Surely, this world has deceived us and busied us. We have become capricious and astray. O son of this world – easy, easy! O son of this world – reduce, reduce! O son of this world – gather, gather! This world will be annihilated, century after century. Not a day passes except that it weakens our pillars. We have lost the abode that remains, and we have taken residence in the abode that perishes. We will not know what we have left until we die.” Al-Harith said: O Amir al-Mu’minin! Do the Christians know this? He said: Had they known this, they would not have taken the Messiah as a god besides Allah.  He said: So, I went to the monk and I said to him: By the right that the Messiah has upon you – strike the bell from the side that you have struck it.   He said: So, he began striking it, and I said [the earlier saying] letter by letter until I reached “until we die.” So, he said: By the right of your Prophet – who informed you of this? I said: The man who was with me yesterday. So, he said: Does he have a relation to the Prophet? I said: He is his cousin. He said: By the right of your Prophet – did he hear this from your Prophet? He said: I said: Yes. So, he converted to Islam, then said to me: By Allah! I saw in the Torah that there will be a final prophet who will interpret what the bell says.
